name: Cepheus
introduction: is the King of Ethiopia, husband of Cassiopeia and father of Andromeda. His stars form a shape like a child’s drawing of a house, lying between Cassiopeia and the Little Dipper. From mid-northern latitudes, Cepheus never sets.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: A faint star at the base of the house, Delta Cephei, changed our view of the universe. Its regular pulsations, discovered by John Goodricke in 1784, define the Cepheid variables. In the 1910s, Henrietta Leavitt found that brighter Cepheids pulsate more slowly. That made them distance markers, which Edwin Hubble later used to show that other galaxies lie far beyond the Milky Way.
Nearby, Mu Cephei, the Garnet Star, as William Herschel called it, is a deep red supergiant and one of the largest stars visible to the naked eye.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alderamin](hip:105199), the brightest star, spins rapidly and is only 49 light-years away. Precession will make it the pole star around AD 7500. [Errai](hip:116727) will take that role even sooner, around AD 4000. It is a binary star with a giant planet, one of the first planets ever suspected around another star.

[Alfirk](hip:106032) is the prototype of the Beta Cephei variables, hot stars that pulsate every few hours. The red dwarf pair [Kruger 60](id:10pc-0061), only 13 light-years away, also lies within Cepheus.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Clouds of gas and dust, including the [Cepheus clouds](id:cahlon-cloud-56), are forming new stars here. Among them glow the Iris Nebula and the Elephant’s Trunk, a dark finger of gas in the large IC 1396 nebula. On the border with Cygnus, the Fireworks Galaxy, NGC 6946, has produced ten supernovae in a century.
